title: Dependability engagement canvas and milestone schedule (2026)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This working doc is the engagement canvas and milestone schedule for the cross-functional dependability program focused on service-level objectives (SLOs), operational runbooks, and rollout patterns for Q2–Q4 2026. Primary audience: platform-engineering, site-reliability-engineering, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, and solutions-engineering leads. Use this as the coordination artifact for weekly syncs and the decision ledger for milestone gating.

High-level objective (north star):
Reduce customer-impacting reliability incidents by 45% for model-serving endpoints by end of Q4 2026 while keeping median 95th-token latency within current SLOs and lowering p95 tail latency variance by 20%. Achieve predictable error budget spend across feature launches with standardized SLO contracts and a lightweight rollout guard.

What this doc contains (quick index):
- Engagement canvas (owners, stakeholders, decision points)
- 6-month milestone schedule with sprint buckets and owners
- SLO templates and suggested thresholds per service class
- Runbook and fallback-patterns summary (canary, graceful degradation)
- Risk register and dependency map (critical cross-team touchpoints)
- Weekly cadence and meeting expectations (artifacts to produce)
- Unresolved questions and open actions (decision ledger)

Engagement canvas (who does what)
- Program lead: Maya Thompson (platform-engineering) — overall schedule, cross-org comms, exec reporting.
- SRE lead: Arjun Rao (site-reliability-engineering) — SLO measurement, alerting, error-budget dashboarding.
- Serving runtime lead: Lena Morales — kernel selection telemetry, canary control-plane hooks.
- Product lead (hosted-api): Ethan Brooks — consumer contracts, rollout gating for public API changes.
- Solutions / CS liaison: Sofia Chen — customer impact quantification, pilot participants.
- Data/observability: Clara Nguyen — telemetry pipeline, tracing augmentation, and cost-per-token dashboards.

Decision authority matrix (RACI-light)
- SLO thresholds for a service: R=SRE lead, A=Program lead, C=product owner, I=exec (quarterly).
- Rollout gating policy: R=Serving runtime + SRE, A=product lead, C=platform eng, I=security/compliance for private deployments.
- Emergency fallback path (capacity or model variant): R=Serving runtime lead, A=SRE lead, C=platform eng ops.

Milestone schedule (quarterly buckets + sprint map)
- Q2 2026 (Discovery + pilot):
  - Weeks 11–14: Inventory & classification of model-serving surfaces by customer impact (owner: product) — deliverable: dependency matrix CSV (PLAT-889).
  - Weeks 15–18: Define SLO family taxonomy (latency token-level, availability, quality proxy) and create baseline measurements (owner: SRE) — deliverable: SLO baseline dashboard.
  - Weeks 19–22: Pick two pilot services (low-risk + mid-risk) for rollout of new SLO guard and canary pattern (owners: serving runtime + product) — deliverable: pilot runbooks and canary config.
- Q3 2026 (Implementation + tool integration):
  - Weeks 23–30: Implement error-budget and SLO alerting in observability stack; wire prefix/KV cache metrics into dashboards (owner: observability/data) — deliverable: alert recipes and runbook steps.
  - Weeks 31–34: Platform autoscaling and cost guard integration for dedicated pools; create capacity fallbacks (owner: platform-eng) — deliverable: autoscale policy templates.
  - Weeks 35–38: Internal rollout to canary group of feature teams; capture regressions and iterate SLO thresholds (owner: product + SRE) — deliverable: canary retrospective and threshold updates.
- Q4 2026 (Rollout + governance):
  - Weeks 39–44: Full rollout to high-traffic services with per-route dashboards and owner sign-off (owners: product + platform) — deliverable: sign-off checklist.
  - Weeks 45–52: Governance embedding (SLO review cadence, quarterly audits, training docs for feature teams) — deliverable: SLO cookbook and onboarding materials.

SLO templates (quick start)
- Low-impact / internal: availability=99.0% monthly, latency median < 20ms, p95 < 90ms. Alert: when 7-day rolling error budget burn > 30%.
- Production-serving (customer-facing, model generation): availability=99.5% monthly, latency p50 < 50ms, p95 < 250ms. Alert: when error budget burn > 20% in 24h window or consecutive degradation of p95 over three 1h windows.
- Latency-sensitive endpoints (real-time agents): availability=99.9% monthly, p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms. Alert: immediate paging when p95 > threshold for >10min plus increased error budget projection.
Notes: Quality proxies (BLEU-like or embedding-similarity regressions) are secondary SLOs and live in the Optimize product area; any quality SLO breach triggers human review and possible rollback of model variant.

Runbook patterns and fallback strategies
- Canary blue/green with pinned model variant: deploy 1% traffic, monitor latency/p95, error budget; if within thresholds, increment to 5%, 20%, 100%. Abort if error-budget burn exceeds threshold or p95 spike beyond allowed multiplier.
- Graceful degradation: when KV cache misses spike or backend tf-serving queues grow > 70%, degrade to reduced-context mode (drop heavy-context features) and serve with cached responses for known prefixes.
- Model variant fallback: automatically route to CPU-quantized variant or smaller model shelf with configured latency/cost contract. Note: require product sign-off for quality delta.

Telemetry & observability requirements
- Key metrics: request rate, token-per-request distribution, p50/p95/p99 latency, error budget burn rate, model-variant route ratios, cache hit ratio, queue depth.
- Traces: include model_id, kernel_path, sequence_length, batch_size.
- Dashboards: per-route, per-model, per-customer (for pilot customers).

Dependency map (top risks)
- Observability pipeline lag: if metrics are >2m delayed, SLO enforcement is ineffective. Mitigation: short retention stream for alerts, sampling fallback. Owner: data/observability.
- Capacity shortage in Dedicated pools: mitigation: reserve emergency burst nodes and fast fallback routing policy to other regions. Owner: platform eng.
- Customer consent for quality fallbacks in Private deployments: mitigation: pre-negotiated contractual clauses and CS liaison. Owner: solutions-eng + legal.

Weekly cadence and artifacts
- Weekly cross-functional sync (Wed 9:30–10:00 PT): agenda = blockers, milestone progress, decision requests. Required artifacts: updated milestone board (sheet), latest canary metrics snapshot, open decision ledger.
- Biweekly SLO design review with feature teams: deep dives on SLO thresholds and customer impact (owner: SRE).
- Monthly exec readout: two-slide summary (status, risks, next milestones).

Decision ledger (open items)
- D1 (owner: product): final SLO threshold for hosted-generation p95 — due 2026-05-10.
- D2 (owner: platform): acceptable p99 tail multiplier to trigger automatic rollback — due 2026-06-01.
- D3 (owner: legal/solutions): template language for quality fallback consent in private deployments — due 2026-07-15.

Open questions and notes to resolve
- How to reliably measure "quality proxy" for multimodal endpoints in an automated, low-latency way? (SRE + Optimize to prototype)
- Should we expose error-budget APIs to customers for self-service dashboards? Pros/cons and security review needed.
- Experiment: two-tier SLOs for conversational workloads (latency vs. quality) — need product prioritization.

Immediate next actions (first 30 days)
- Maya: publish shared milestone board and invite leads to weekly sync (done).
- Arjun: create baseline SLO dashboards for the two pilot services (SRE-1423).
- Lena: prototype canary hook that can read error-budget projection and abort rollout (PR: platform/pull/542).
- Clara: wire minimal tracing tags (model_id, sequence_length) into sampling pipeline for pilot customers.

Appendix: useful links and references
- Confluence: Dependability Initiative Portal (linked above)
- Jira: SRE-1423 (pilot SLOs), PLAT-889 (inventory), SERV-601 (canary control-plane work)
- Slack channels: #reliability-ops, #platform-rollouts, #serving-runtime-canaries

Notes on tone: this is a working coaching/coordination doc — expect churn. Add concrete minutes and decision notes into the decision ledger section when decisions are made.

Unpublished/privileged: none — safe to share within Redwood engineering + CS.
